I'm checking the error message by reasoning, because Bash is disabled here and I can't run `python3 -I`. I also found no journal or manifest files in the directory.

ROOT CAUSE: There are two separate faults in `scripts/wf_run.py`. The first causes the parse failures. The second causes the "budget" label. Neither was reproduced by running code.

(a) `WorkflowEngine.agent()` (around lines 796–815) sets `current_prompt = rendered`. The schema is not in that prompt. `_schema_retry_prompt` appends it only after a `schema_invalid` result. `run_claude` in `wf_adapters.py` passes no schema flag either. So on attempt 1 the model gets no format instruction and answers in prose or a markdown fence. `_parse_and_validate` (line 217) then calls `json.loads(result.text)`, which raises "Expecting value" at line 1, column 1. If the text is empty, it fails the same way. This matches all three tasks failing identically at column 1. The fix is to include the schema in the first prompt.

(b) `Budget.exhausted()` (line 136) returns true when `dispatched_calls >= maximum_calls`. The loop at lines 819–829 checks it before each attempt. Three tasks each used one dispatch, so `dispatched_calls` reached 3, which equals `max_calls=3`. Each retry was then journaled as `retry_deferred` with reason "budget" and `partial_reason` was set to "budget" (lines 821, 922). The check never separates the call cap from the USD cap, so the label is wrong. Only 0.016 of 3 USD was spent.

(a) causes (b): the first attempts failed parsing, so each task needed a retry, and the retries hit the exhausted call cap.
